decisions.executionNote: Raise both arms into continuous elbow-up approaches; plan pens in white, watches in blue, cameras in red. Initial geometry uncertain.
Approach left pen and inner right camera from above, increasing downward tool pitch while retaining elbow-up branches.
Align closing directions across the horizontal pen and camera; finish downward approach orientation before lowering.
Correct alignment from wrist views: forward over pen, inward and forward over camera, with a cautious descent.
Lower toward grasp height, centering the camera deeper between the fingers and refining pen lateral alignment.
Close on the pen and begin a small retention lift; recenter the camera after apparent contact before closing the right gripper.
Lift both closed grippers vertically to verify pen and camera retention before basket transport.
Both objects appear retained. Carry pen toward white basket and camera toward red, staying on each arm's own side.
Replan from interrupted pose: lower and slightly tilt forward to place objects inside baskets without extending the high approach further.
Open over white and red baskets, pause for release, then withdraw upward and back to inspect settling.
Withdraw toward green watch with left arm and remaining camera with right; restore vertical grasp orientation. Released objects appear inside assigned baskets.
Descend over watch and second camera; align right fingers with the camera's diagonal long axis, using RGB geometry for centering.
Refine watch and camera centering from wrist views, lower the last centimeters, and close both grippers.
Lift the green watch and second camera with grippers closed; verify retention before moving toward their baskets.
Watch was not retained; reopen and recenter lower for another grasp. Carry retained camera toward red basket with a slight forward tilt to limit extension.
Target the solid watch face rather than the hollow band and grasp lower. Lower and release the second camera inside red basket.
Test watch retention with a short vertical lift; withdraw the open right gripper from the two cameras now visible in red basket.
Watch remains on table. Reopen above it, shift toward the visible solid dial, and approach lower without closing prematurely.
Close around the solid green dial and test a short lift. Move the right arm toward the remaining white pen while keeping clear of the left workspace.
Lift the apparently retained watch clear of the table; approach the white pen with the right gripper aligned across its axis.
Transport retained watch toward blue basket with a forward tilt for reach margin. Center the right gripper on the white pen and descend to grasp height.
Move the watch fully over blue basket before opening. Close on the centered white pen and lift it vertically for retention verification.
Withdraw left toward the silver watch. Carry retained white pen to a central staging area for left-side pickup without crossing either arm.
Approach the silver watch's solid case with left fingers. Lower white pen onto the central-front table, separated from the watch approach.
Release the staged white pen and retract rightward. Aim left fingers at the silver watch case, rather than the hollow strap, with a slow final descent.
Center the silver watch case and close for a short retention lift. Begin retracting the open right arm toward its home configuration.
Lift and move slightly left to check whether the silver watch follows the gripper; continue the right arm's gradual return toward origin.
Silver watch did not follow the lift. Reopen and approach its case lower; finish the right arm's gradual return to its starting pose.
Lower slightly farther around the silver watch case, then close and make a small test lift. Right arm remains open near origin.
Test silver-watch retention with a vertical lift and small leftward displacement; do not infer success from closure alone.
Silver watch remains on table. Reopen and approach with the case farther toward the fingertip contact zone, correcting the prior overly deep image placement.
Close with the silver dial centered near the finger tips, then lift only a few centimeters to check retention.
Lift the silver watch and begin a small forward carry, checking that it stays between the fingers; tilt slightly forward for basket reach margin.
Silver watch is visibly retained. Carry it over the blue basket, lowering and tilting modestly to preserve extension margin.
Replan after continuity interruption: lower and tilt from the observed pose, moving only slightly forward, then release silver watch inside blue basket.
Both watches are visible inside blue basket. Withdraw the open left gripper upward and backward toward the staged white pen; keep right arm at origin.
Approach the left end of the staged white pen from above, aligning finger closure across its axis while keeping the left EE on its own side.
Center the white pen laterally in the left wrist view and lower cautiously for a grasp near its left end; right arm remains clear at origin.
The pen is offset from the contact zone. Tilt the left tool toward its shaft while keeping the EE left of center; make a small lateral correction without closing.
Close across the white pen shaft after a final small alignment correction, then make a short vertical retention test.
Lift and carry the apparently retained white pen leftward toward the white basket, keeping the gripper closed and the right arm clear.
White pen is retained. Carry it toward the white basket, gently restoring a forward-tilted downward orientation for reach margin.
Advance the retained white pen fully over the white basket and lower gently, with a small forward tilt to avoid overextension.
Release the white pen into the white basket, pause for settling, and withdraw the open left gripper clear of the rim before returning home.
All six objects appear in category-specific baskets. Begin a gradual elbow-up return of the left arm, with a small right-home correction; keep both grippers open.
Continue the smooth left-arm return, reducing tool rotation and elbow flexion while staying clear of the sorted objects.
Complete the gradual return to the initial poses with both grippers open; objects remain visually grouped in their baskets.
